s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging facial swelling with bony destruction
salient_findings: Diffuse, firm, non-tender mass on the left cheek
Vestibular swelling extending from the distal aspect of the left canine to the second molar
Bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old South Asian man
3-month history of gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek
Mass measures about 4 × 5 cm
Mass extends from the infraorbital region to the lip commissure
Mass obliterates the nasal ala medially and approaches the preauricular area laterally
Intraoral examination reveals a well-defined vestibular swelling
Vestibular swelling measures 4 × 3 cm
Routine hematologic parameters are within normal limits
Contrast-enhanced CT shows a mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion
Incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common malignancy of the head and neck region

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with potential for facial involvement

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Soft tissue sarcoma that can occur in the head and neck

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with facial swelling and bony destruction

shortlist.label: Fibrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can occur in the head and neck region

raw.rationale: The incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, which is more consistent with lymphoma, and the clinical presentation of a rapidly enlarging mass with adjacent bony destruction is also plausible for lymphoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the biopsy results do not specifically suggest squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Malignant melanoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of pigmentation or other characteristic features of melanoma in the clinical description.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results suggest myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, not rhabdomyosarcoma, which is a type of sarcoma.

rejected.label: Fibrosarcoma
rejected.why: The clinical and biopsy findings do not specifically support fibrosarcoma, which would typically show different histological features.
